mock_exam.weighting_note: 70% current module (21Q on M5 — all 12 items from levels 21-24 are included in full, since those levels fall past the last checkpoint at level 20 and would otherwise go untested; 9 more spread across levels 1-20 for breadth) / 30% Phase 2 review (9Q on M4, 6 of them gender-flagged exception words — gender is now an 'older high-value concept' worth re-testing in every module going forward).
mock_exam.structural_note: Module 5 has 24 levels, not a multiple of 5, so its 4 checkpoints (after L5/10/15/20) leave levels 21-24 (negation, word order, connectors) uncovered by any checkpoint. Compensated the same way as Modules 3 and 14: full mock coverage of those levels.

questions.prompt_en: Which of these is the grammatically correct sentence?
questions.explanation_en: नहीं goes immediately before the verb, not before the adjective.

questions.prompt_en: Which of these is the grammatically correct sentence?
questions.explanation_en: नहीं comes before the verb, never after it. Dropping the verb is fine; moving it is not.

questions.prompt_en: Which of these is the grammatically correct sentence?
questions.explanation_en: जी comes first in this fixed pair, exactly as it does in जी हाँ.

questions.prompt_en: Which of these is the grammatically correct sentence?
questions.explanation_en: For ordinary negation use नहीं. न in that slot sounds formal or poetic rather than neutral.

questions.prompt_en: Which of these is the grammatically correct sentence?
questions.explanation_en: Commands take मत, not नहीं. The two are not interchangeable in either direction.

questions.prompt_en: Which of these is the grammatically correct sentence?
questions.explanation_en: मत only negates commands. A statement always takes नहीं.

questions.prompt_en: Which of these is the grammatically correct sentence?
questions.explanation_en: The verb goes last in Hindi, so nothing may follow it.

questions.prompt_en: Which of these is the grammatically correct sentence?
questions.explanation_en: किताब is feminine, so नया has to take its irregular feminine form नई.

questions.prompt_en: Which of these is the grammatically correct sentence?
questions.explanation_en: The verb stays at the end in questions too. Only क्या is added, and only at the front.

questions.prompt_en: Which of these is the grammatically correct sentence?
options: चाय गरम है लेकिन ठंडी नहीं है।
चाय गरम है और ठंडी है।
questions.explanation_en: और joins things that agree with each other. A contradiction needs लेकिन.

questions.prompt_en: Which of these is the grammatically correct sentence?
options: चाय अच्छी है क्योंकि गरम है।
चाय गरम है क्योंकि अच्छी है।
questions.explanation_en: क्योंकि introduces the reason, so the reason has to be the clause that follows it.

questions.prompt_en: Which of these is the grammatically correct sentence?
questions.explanation_en: क्योंकि has to be followed by a reason and cannot be left at the end of a sentence.

questions.prompt_en: Which of these is the grammatically correct sentence?
options: चाय गरम है और ठंडी है।
questions.explanation_en: बच्चे is masculine plural, so the adjective takes -े just as the verb takes हैं.

questions.prompt_en: Which of these is the grammatically correct sentence?
questions.explanation_en: यह is singular, so the verb is है. The respectful version would use ये कौन हैं?

questions.prompt_en: Which of these is the grammatically correct sentence?
questions.explanation_en: चाय is feminine, so the form has to agree with it just as an adjective would.

questions.prompt_en: Which of these is the grammatically correct sentence?
questions.explanation_en: बड़ा agrees because it ends in -ा; साफ़ does not, so adding an ending to it is wrong.

questions.prompt_en: Which of these is the grammatically correct sentence?
questions.explanation_en: If the verb is plural the adjective must be too. वो itself gives you no clue either way, so the rest of the sentence has to be consistent.

questions.prompt_en: Which of these is the grammatically correct sentence?
questions.explanation_en: Both the adjective and the verb agree with चाय, so both have to be feminine.

questions.prompt_en: Which of these is the grammatically correct sentence?
questions.explanation_en: The subject is plural, so the verb must be plural too.

questions.prompt_en: Which of these is the grammatically correct sentence?
options: चाय गरम है क्योंकि अच्छी है।
questions.explanation_en: वह is singular, so the verb is है. A postposition does not change the agreement.

questions.prompt_en: Which of these is the grammatically correct sentence?
questions.explanation_en: आप takes हैं. Mixing आप with हो sounds like you began respectfully and gave up halfway through.
